title: Most horns are logarithmic spirals from constant unequal growth on opposite sides

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Most horns are logarithmic spirals from constant unequal growth on opposite sides

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In the great majority of horns the curve is a continuous logarithmic spiral, caused by unequal rates of growth parallel to the axis on opposite sides of the horn, the inequality keeping a constant ratio throughout growth.

fields.label: Notation
fields.value: v_1/v_2 = \text{const} on opposite sides of the axis \Rightarrow r = a e^{\theta\cot\alpha}

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. XIII: The Shapes of Horns, and of Teeth or Tusks: with a Note on Torsion

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: But in the great majority of horns, we have no difficulty in recognising a continuous logarithmic spiral, nor in referring it, as before, to an unequal rate of growth (parallel to the axis) on two opposite sides of the horn, the inequality maintaining a constant ratio as long as growth proceeds.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter XIII, “The Shapes of Horns, and of Teeth or Tusks: with a Note on Torsion”; topic “Spiral angle of horns”. Scope: horns of hollow-horned ruminants

fields.label: Notation
fields.value: v_1/v_2 = \text{const} on opposite sides of the axis \Rightarrow r = a e^{\theta\cot\alpha}

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch13-03: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.73

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The geometric majority claim can be tested now with public specimen media and standard curve model comparison. The specific constant-growth mechanism is only partially covered, but a strong geometric rejection would resolve the compound assertion.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Fit logarithmic and rival curves to horn centerlines across Bovidae and estimate opposite-side longitudinal increments from annuli where visible. Majority support requires stable logarithmic parameters and near-constant growth asymmetry through ontogeny; widespread better alternatives or ratio drift refutes it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
External geometry is much more available than side-specific growth increments.

The phrase 'great majority' requires representative taxonomic sampling.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Whether most horns are logarithmic spirals is decidable by curve-fitting on existing scans and photographs, and the methods are standard. The causal clause, a constant ratio of growth on opposite sides, is the geometric meaning Thompson gives the spiral rather than a separate measured growth field. Taxonomic coverage is broad enough for a majority claim about well-collected bovids and incomplete for the family as a whole, and it does not separate growth from later mechanical retardation.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Fit logarithmic, circular, and piecewise spirals to horn centerlines from bovid scans and test whether one angle is constant along the horn. A majority of horns with a stable logarithmic angle would support the geometric claim; a better fit by curves whose curvature changes with length would refute it. Unequal axial growth remains identified with that angle unless increment thicknesses are measured around the base.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Constant unequal growth and some adhesion patterns produce the same logarithmic centerline.

Open meshes are biased toward species with skeletal specimens and often lack the keratin sheath.
